title: Rural well interference appeal committee approved
subtitle: Also: Ira Needles resurfacing, police CCTV cameras, Doon Heritage Village reopening, Blair traffic review, water capacity.
overview: Council directed staff to design a Council-appointed Well Interference Appeal Committee for residents on private wells who believe Regional pumping has affected their water {{vote:m19}}. Staff will report to the August 12, 2026 Special Council Water meeting. Pending that, residents with open complaints about the K50, K51 and K52 wells are not to be asked to sign a full release to get temporary water support. Surface water was removed from the scope.

Council also approved adding Ira Needles Boulevard resurfacing to the 2026 capital budget {{vote:m14}}, an agreement for police CCTV cameras on Regional infrastructure {{vote:m10}}, and free, donation-based admission to the July 1 Doon Heritage Village reopening {{vote:m15}}. A traffic and safety review of the Blair Village area was sent to the Integrated Mobility Plan {{vote:m17}}.

Council ratified two appointments to the Sunnyside Foundation Board after a closed session {{vote:m13}}. A request to waive notice for a motion to reconsider Standing Committee Chair pay was defeated {{vote:m23}}, so that item was not debated. Delegates also raised Mannheim water capacity, which staff will address on June 3.

decisions.detail: Staff are directed to bring a report and draft policy to the August 12, 2026 Special Council Water meeting to replace the current appeal process with a Council-appointed committee, with a review path for K50, K51 and K52 complaints since 2019.

The Commissioner of Transportation Services may sign an agreement with the Waterloo Regional Police Service Board for CCTV cameras on Regional lands and infrastructure, with no installation on Regional infrastructure unless the area municipality has an agreement.
Resurfacing between Yellow Birch Drive and West Hill Drive is added to the 2026 capital budget at an estimated $4.5 million from the Transportation Capital Reserve.
Admission to the July 1, 2026 reopening event is waived and replaced by optional donation, with no suggested amount.
Staff will review traffic and safety in Blair Village, Fountain Street, Shantz Hill Road and the King Street connections through the Integrated Mobility Plan, including past by-pass studies.

Council exempted income-eligible households permanently, and the first 50 other households temporarily, from the $450 RetrofitWR fee, and referred a special hospital levy equal to 0.5% of the tax-supported budget to the 2027 base budget.

decisions.item: Victoria Street expropriation and facilities plan
decisions.detail: Council approved expropriating land for Victoria Street South improvements in Kitchener and declared Cambridge road lands surplus for sale. It also funded a Corporate Facilities Strategic Plan at $350,000.
The 2026 Children's Services operating budget rises by $7,879,158 to reflect Ministry of Education funding changes, with no net tax levy impact.

debate: Delegates supporting a well interference committee said the Region both operates the wells and decides complaints, which they called a conflict of interest. They described wells running dry, a $4,000 compensation offer tied to a release, and denials without baseline data. One delegate wanted township mayors on the committee rather than urban councillors, and a councillor questioned how elected members fit an independent, expert-led body.

On timing, staff said the current policy is outdated and a proper review needs consultation and an outside consultant, and preferred a fall report. Councillors wanted a faster date because residents were affected now. Staff said fewer consultation rounds would make August workable, and council chose August 12. Staff also said surface water is outside Regional jurisdiction, and it was removed.

On CCTV, a councillor raised accountability, bias in identification and over-surveillance. Police described privacy review, a board policy, training, auditing, quarterly reporting and public camera locations. Council added a condition that no cameras go on Regional infrastructure without an agreement with the area municipality.

On Ira Needles, one councillor asked why not repair now and wait for the 2027 budget. Staff said local repairs would cost about $700,000 this year and the full work would still follow, and that a tender award report will return to Council.

A home builders' delegate argued the proposed 20% resiliency factor creates a water deficit and should be phased in. Staff said that factor is under review in a framework due June 3, and a councillor asked that the report be public well ahead of the meeting.
